purpose: Physical router requested-heap anatomy of the accepted Client and an alternative boxed table value; no daemon traffic or performance acceptance.
measurement: Real socket pairs and Client constructors; separately count credential/group heap, value wrapper heap and HashMap backing storage. Count current requested bytes and construction peak. Clear/drop assertions require exact recovery. No rx buffers are allocated.
production: C only; guarded disposable namespace; benchmark uses socket pairs. R109 ELF is uploaded as a harness identity anchor but not executed. Every usual before/after health/config/boot/mount/identity and cleanup check is mandatory.
limits: Requested Rust heap, not malloc class sizes, RSS, PSS, kernel/socket memory or process peak.
Boxed representation is measured only as an isolated container; no inference that its extra pointer/allocations improve daemon performance.
Actual retained rx buffers and other daemon registries are not included.
